title: Interactive Gambling and Broadcasting Amendment (Online Transactions and Other Measures) Bill 2011 [2013]
short_title: Interactive Gambling and Broadcasting Amendment (Online Transactions and Other Measures) Bill 2011 [2013]

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would restrict certain betting services, gambling promotions and broadcasts, allow customers to request that unfinished interactive gambling payments be stopped, and create an offence covering match-fixing.
It would use corporate betting prohibitions, broadcaster licence conditions and changes to gambling and criminal laws, with detailed betting definitions set through regulations.
The proposal would cover commercial television, radio and subscription television, with commencement on the 28th day after royal assent to the bill is given.
changes: Corporations would be barred from offering spot, exotic, in-play and similar betting, with those forms defined by regulation.
Customers could request suspension or cancellation of an unfinished interactive gambling payment, with financial transaction providers protected from liability for stopping it.
Certain chance-based games intended to induce later gambling would be treated as prohibited gambling services.
Broadcasters could not advertise betting venues or online gambling sites during G-classified, sports or sports-related programs.
Licence conditions would also prohibit broadcasting betting odds supplied under commercial arrangements involving broadcasters or their agents.
Match-fixing involving financial advantage by deception would carry maximum penalties of 10 years' imprisonment, 10,000 penalty units, or both.
summary.affected: Gambling corporations, customers, financial transaction providers, commercial and subscription broadcasters, players, referees and other people associated with sporting codes are affected.
